Their perception of whether this belief is socially desirable (which may cause them to hide their true estimate or adjust it upward/downward to match perceived norms)

Women may estimate lower consensus (due to personal disagreement and exposure to gender discrimination) or potentially higher consensus if they perceive patriarchal barriers as widely accepted. Men may overestimate agreement due to in-group bias.
Older respondents may perceive higher consensus reflecting traditional norms; younger respondents may project liberalization trends or underestimate conservative sentiment.
Higher education correlates with egalitarian attitudes and exposure to global norms, likely lowering estimates of agreement.
